source.filename: The Status Game On Social Position and How We Use It (Will Storr) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).epub
source.edition: William Collins, first Great Britain ebook publication 2021; Ebook Edition August 2021; Version 2021-08-25

scope: Extended thematic summary based on review across all 29 chapters, including full extracted text review of chapters 1, 2, 4, 5, 11, 12, 21, and 29. Other chapters reviewed through representative substantive passages; not an exhaustive paragraph-by-paragraph review of the complete ebook.
location_convention: EPUB spine indices are zero-based. Chapter numbers refer to the supplied edition. EPUB hrefs locate the source documents. No PDF or printed page numbers have been fabricated.

coverage.review: full extracted text; author acknowledges limits, disagreement, and potentially superseded findings

exclusions.reason: Endnotes and bibliography not systematically reviewed or independently verified; no new outside research added.
Cover, dedication, epigraph, index, acknowledgements, author biography, other works, and publisher details excluded from substantive summary.

limitations: Reflowable EPUB supplied instead of PDF: provenance uses source chapter/document locations and has no fixed page mapping.
Chapter-spanning review was selective outside the fully reviewed chapters listed in scope. A chapter reference locates support and does not assert every paragraph was reviewed.

Native XHTML extraction required no OCR. Initial extraction of headings, paragraphs, and list items omitted some standalone block text. Body-text audit and follow-up inspection recovered the substantial omitted passages in chapters 4 and 28; small token differences elsewhere may include inline word splits or navigation text.
Historical and psychological explanations are attributed to Storr; this summary does not independently validate the cited research or update it beyond the supplied 2021 edition.

The supplied ebook remains the authority for the full-book conversion; its complete text was separately checked by native RTF round-trip comparison. This conversion check is not a claim of exhaustive editorial reading.

reading_time.included: synopsis, section titles, and section bodies

sections.support: Belonging versus rank, local standing, and wellbeing findings.

sections.title: Meaning is often built inside a local world
sections.support: Ben Gunn’s prison identity, preparation for release, public writing, and loss of a respected role.

sections.title: The mind tells a flattering story about the contest
sections.support: Self-serving stories, symbolic signals, comparison, and relative income.

sections.title: Cultures teach us what deserves recognition
sections.support: Hidden cultural rules, pub etiquette, collective and individual status, childhood socialisation, personality, and opportunity.

sections.title: Dominance virtue and success are three overlapping strategies
sections.support: Three status strategies, prestige, useful contributions, and mixed games.

sections.title: Prestige helps knowledge spread and can spread error too
sections.support: Prestige cues, imitation, reputation, gossip, and attention feedback.

sections.title: Organisations shape character through their daily rewards

sections.title: Threat can produce a competition in moral purity

sections.title: A monopoly over identity makes a group dangerous

sections.title: Better rules can direct ambition toward discovery

sections.title: Merit depends on opportunity and the modern game distributes both unevenly
